ELI5: How the USD became the world's preeminent forex currency.

Usa has the biggest economy. People want to go there. People want to sell their shit there. USA sort of controls a huge chunk of the world economy because they consume the most. The poor want to be it, the rich can't argue with it.

Simple answer - Because it was (and overall, still is) the most STABLE currency.

For businesses the currency of the people or company they're dealing with can go up or down. That means that one of the two parties could get a better or worse deal depending on what the two currencies do in the time between agreeing on a deal and the actual date of payment. To minimize that gamble they simply do business in the most stable currency.

If you're asking about people or travelers who want to exchange their currency for a different country's currency, and are asking why all the currencies are compared to the USD, there again it comes down to the USD being the most stable. So a foreign exchange will trade one currency for another, and now they're stuck with that second currency which can drop in value and the exchange itself will loose. So to lower that risk they reference everything to the most stable currency, the USD.

And yes the value of the USD does go up and down, but overall it's the most stable compared to other currencies. The reason it's the most stable is that the economy and country itself is so big. If there's a drought in California you can sill have a bumper crop in Nebraska. Or if the lumber industry suffers losses, it doesn't mean the steel industry will. The economy is more diverse than almost all others and that adds to it's so stablity.

Unconditional Basic Income is a horrible idea. In order for wealth to be generated, you need land and labor, which creates production. Paying people to not labor doesn't generate wealth, as the market simply shifts (inflation). In this case, it's simply bottom up inflation rather than top down. Think about it; if every landlord in your city knows you're going to have at least X amount of dollars every month, he's going to charge you as much as he thinks he can get away with. The local government knows you're going to have more money, which means more fees, charges, and fines. The police will create more traffic stops, etc etc. It will inevitably become more expensive to live since those with the power to extract wealth know there is a guaranteed amount of wealth to be had.

Yes, these people will have money but, they did not produce any kind of wealth through the act of labor itself. It was given to them.This creates an inevitable drain upon the wealth generated by everyone else, as a portion of that will have to be given to those who aren't producing.

Despite people having more money on paper, in reality it will be much more difficult to meet one's economic needs. Basic income is an idea that has its merits in regards to those who have contributed a great deal but are no longer able to commit to labor (wounded veterans, first responders, police, doctor injured while administering aid, and so on), or for those people who were born without the ability to labor through age, genetics, or severe physical or mental trauma.

It's not a concept that can be applied to the overall economic system of a nation though, because when we guarantee that individuals have wealth by whatever virtue, we end up creating what could be considered "economic prey". Who are some of the biggest victims of grifts, scams, and deception? Old people, veterans, the disabled, the mentally handicapped, i.e. those who fall under the merits of basic income. It's why we find such crimes even more morally reprehensible than just outright theft or burglary.

You see the same phenomenon among college students who have just received fresh students loans, as they are easy prey for banks, retailers, and frivolous services.

We instinctively get that people who must be provided for are unable to do so for themselves, and when people see weakness, they take advantage of it. It's why we have laws to protect those of us who have been given aid in the first place.

It makes no sense to put able bodied people into that category, even with economic downturns. The solutions to such problems lie elsewhere. Any attempt to incorporate a basic income into an economic system will result in a market and financial environment more predatory than anything we've ever seen.
